claim: Cap Canaille reaches 394 m and is described as the highest sea cliff of France, with the Corniche des Crêtes scenic road running over the top.
quote: At 394 m (1,293 ft), it is the highest sea cliff of France. ... The Corniche des Crêtes scenic road runs over the top of the cliff.

claim: Route des Crêtes is automatically closed on red-fire-risk days between 1 June and 30 September and is often very congested in summer.
quote: Route des Crêtes is automatically closed on days classified as red for fire danger between 1 June and 30 September ... When stopping on Route des Crêtes, do not approach the edge. Sudden wind can cause falls.

claim: The Soubeyranes cliffs extend roughly 4 km from Cap Canaille to the Sémaphore du Bec de l'Aigle and rank among the highest sea cliffs in Europe, peaking at 394 m.
quote: Les falaises Soubeyranes s'étendent sur environ 4 km, de Cap Canaille au sémaphore du Bec de l'Aigle ... parmi les plus hautes falaises maritimes d'Europe, avec un sommet culminant à 394 mètres.

claim: The Grotte Sainte-Madeleine + Saint-Pilon loop from the Hôtellerie de la Sainte Baume car park is 3.94 mi, +1,230 ft elevation, ~2h55, moderate difficulty.
quote: Distance: 3.94 mi ... + 1,230 ft ... 2h 55 ... Moderate ... Hôtellerie de la Sainte Baume car park

claim: The Grotte Sainte-Marie-Madeleine sits about a 45-minute climb above the Hôtellerie via a path lined with stations of the Crucifixion; cave temperature is a constant 13°C.
quote: After a climb of about 45 minutes along a winding path and up steps looking out on the life-size depiction of the Crucifixion of Jesus, you arrive at the esplanade of the cave. ... The temperature inside is 13°C, in winter and summer.

claim: Access to Sainte-Baume massifs is regulated by prefectural order June–September and several trails (Pic Noir, Marcel Estruch viewpoint, SB 100 from Auriol) carry separate closures.
quote: Pic Noir Trail remains closed under the February 3, 2023 municipal order from Plan d'Aups Sainte-Baume. ... Marcel Estruch Viewpoint: Access path prohibited indefinitely since May 28, 2019.

claim: Mont Caume tops out at 804 m and is reached via the narrow former military D662 over about 6 km from Col du Corps de Garde on the D62; the summit retains ONF-managed fire-watch structures.
quote: Le Mont Caume culmine à 804m sur les contreforts de la rade de Toulon ... l'ancienne petite route militaire, la D662, pendant environ 6 kilomètres. Elle est particulièrement étroite et ne permet que difficilement de s'y croiser.

claim: Mont Caume's 360° panorama covers the Coudon, Giens peninsula, Îles d'Or, Mont Faron, Toulon roadstead, Saint-Mandrier, Bec de l'Aigle and La Ciotat bay — on a clear day, the Corsican reliefs.
quote: vous aurez une vue vraiment magnifique à la fois sur le Coudon, la presqu'île de Giens, les îles d'Or, le Mont Faron, la rade de Toulon, la presqu'île de Saint-Mandrier, le Baou des 4 Ouros, le bec de l'Aigle, la baie de la Ciotat. Par temps très clair, on peut même apercevoir les reliefs corses.

claim: Gros Cerveau hikes from Sanary/Ollioules offer a blue 8 km/300 m loop (3h30–4h) and a red 13 km/700 m loop (~6h); main attractions are the medieval fort and Bandol-bay panorama.
quote: 8km avec 300m de dénivelé pour une boucle d'environ 3h30 à 4h ... 13km avec 700m de dénivelé pour une boucle d'environ 6h ... une vue panoramique sur la Méditerranée

claim: The Gros Cerveau ridge is connected to the GR51 and crowned by two Séré de Rivières-era forts (the Pointe outwork and the Gros-Cerveau fort) built 1890–1900.
quote: Two defensive fortifications built between 1890 and 1900 by General Séré de Rivières — the Pointe outwork and the Gros-Cerveau fort — are still visible on the ridge.

claim: The Gorges du Destel loop from Ollioules is rated difficult: ~4h30, 300 m gain, with technical chain-equipped passages, rock pools and a slippery scree descent.
quote: Sentier technique, nombreux passages avec des chaînes. Ascension raide, descente dans un pierrier très glissant. ... le parcours se fait dans les gorges. On alterne dalles, vasques, et des goulottes

claim: An easy coastal path links Saint-Cyr/Port de la Madrague through Calanque du Port d'Alon and Engraviers beach to Bandol's Anse de Renecros, with seasonal water and toilets at Port d'Alon.
quote: the calanque de Port d'Alon, with its majestic pine trees, enjoy a swim or a break in the shade before continuing on to Bandol. Water and toilets are available in season.

claim: Komoot's curated gravel guide for the Sainte-Baume lists long quiet-road rides between Aix-en-Provence and Saint-Maximin (~70 km) crossing vineyards and pine forests.
quote: The Sainte-Baume is located between Aix-en-Provence and Toulon ... a 70-kilometre ride from Aix-en-Provence to Saint-Maximin-la-Sainte-Baume, cycling via Pourrières and Rians through wine regions and pine forests.

claim: South Provence Sainte Baume launched 11 signposted gravel routes for 2025 crossing Bandol, Saint-Cyr, La Cadière d'Azur, Le Castellet and Sanary, graded easy to very difficult.
quote: New for 2025, the destination South Provence Sainte Baume defined 11 mountain bike trails called 'Gravel: from the vineyard to the sea in western Var', which cross villages including Bandol, Saint-Cyr-sur-Mer, Cadière d'Azur, Castellet and Sanary-sur-mer.

claim: Cassis-side Calanques access (Port-Miou, Port-Pin, En-Vau) requires reservations in 2026 for the weekend of 20–21 June, then daily 27 June–30 August, plus weekends 5–6 and 12–13 September.
quote: In 2026, reservation is mandatory for the weekend of 20 and 21 June, then from 27 June to 30 August, and then, for the weekends of 5-6 and 12-13 September.
